Rhea (PM): Quick sync thread: customers are asking for an "evidence packaging" feature that combines audit logs + request metadata + signed manifests for legal export. Need to nail mapping to our retention tiers and contract language.
Noah (Eng): Sounds good. We should define a canonical export schema first. JSONL sounds fine; maybe a compressed tarball with a manifest and signature.
Priya (Security): Signed manifest = non-negotiable. We also need deterministic checksums per file and an overall signed root. Chain-of-custody matters for ISO evidence.
Evan (Legal): Customers want exports that are "court-ready". We should confirm file format, signature algorithm (RSA/ECDSA), and include a simple certificate chain. Also retention carve-outs in contracts.
Carmen (CS): Two pilots asked for a UI toggle to put a tenant into "legal hold" so retention pauses or extends automatically. We need a visible indicator and export progress in Console.
Liam (Compliance): For SOC2, auditors expect demonstrable retention enforcement. We should log policy decisions (who toggled, when, reason). Those logs must themselves be retained.
Noah (Eng): Implementation notes: export job will gather records by retention_tag, assemble JSONL shards, compute sha256 per shard, create manifest.json, sign it with service key (and optionally include customer KMS-wrapped key). Offer an option to include a notarization token.
Priya (Security): On KMS/BYOK: customers want their keys to protect payloads at rest AND ensure only they can decrypt exports. Two modes: 1) customer-managed key (BYOK) where we never see plaintext except during export via a wrapped/unwrapped flow, or 2) escrowed wrapping key for archived years. Must require explicit consent for escrow.
Evan (Legal): Agree on consent. Need an explicit consent artifact that can be attached to the manifest (signed consent reference). Drafting clause: "Customer grants Redwood permission to escrow a wrapped copy of the key solely for evidence export, subject to revocation with X-day notice."
Rhea (PM): UX questions: how granular should retention be? per-tenant, per-route, per-log-type? What's the default?
Liam (Compliance): Recommend defaults: tenant-level policy (can override per-route). Default baseline: audit_trail=5y, request_metadata=1y, payloads=90d. Allow enterprise customers to extend.
Carmen (CS): Customers expect clear pricing if they extend beyond baseline. We'll need a pricing doc and a surcharge path.
Noah (Eng): Searchability: For long-retained exports, index only metadata in warm store. Full content goes to cold archive. Query engine should support a preview stream to avoid full restore.
Priya (Security): Threat modeling: export manifests must be tamper-evident. Protect signing keys with HSM. If offering BYOK unwrap for export, require customer-held HSM OR an automated escrow protocol with audit.
Evan (Legal): Also: define subpoena/POC process — who gets notified if law enforcement requests an export? Need playbook and SLA for notification.
Rhea (PM): Launch criteria (proposal): 1) Export schema + manifest spec published; 2) Console legal-hold toggle + user docs; 3) BYOK export flow with opt-in escrow for 2 pilot customers; 4) Pricing + contract addendum drafted; 5) SRE restore drill passed.
Noah (Eng): Tech gating: must have artifact-level checksums, signed manifest, and retrieval workflow tested on 2TB dataset for cold restores.
Priya (Security): Security gating: HSM-backed signing, threat model review completed, explicit opt-in recorded in system.
Evan (Legal): Legal gating: consent language approved, subpoena/playbook vetted, and customer-facing FAQs ready.
Carmen (CS): Pilot gating: 2 pilots (one fintech, one healthcare) must complete end-to-end export and confirm chain-of-custody artifacts.
Liam (Compliance): Operational metrics: export time per GB, manifest verification time, and percentage of exports with successful signature verification. SLOs: export correctness 99.9% per month.
ops-bot: New RFC uploaded: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/evidence-packaging-3301239876 (draft)
Rhea (PM): Timeline idea: RFC + manifest spec this week; alpha export + console toggle in 8 weeks; pilot in 14 weeks; GA in 24 weeks. Pushback?
Noah (Eng): Alpha in 8 is tight but doable if we scope to audit_trail only and stub BYOK unwrap.
Priya (Security): We'll need 2 security sprints for HSM integration. Might push BYOK full unwrap to pilot phase.
Evan (Legal): I'll circulate draft consent + subpoena playbook by EOD Friday.
Carmen (CS): I'll line up pilots and collect success criteria; need a sample export to show during sales cycles.
Liam (Compliance): I'll draft the audit checklist for SOC2 reviewers and include evidence of toggles and retained logs.
Rhea (PM): Risks: key revocation, storage costs, complexity of per-tenant overrides, and legal emergency holds. Mitigations?
Noah (Eng): Key revocation: require recovery path via escrow with customer consent. Storage: cold tier + optional paid replication. Per-tenant overrides: limited to enterprise plans in v1.
Priya (Security): Emergency holds: require legal authorizer workflow with dual approval and audit trail. No silent holds.
Evan (Legal): Add escalation contacts for subpoenas and an embargo workflow for legal holds.
Rhea (PM): Action items: Noah - draft export schema + storage plan (due Fri). Priya - HSM/signing design + threat model (due Fri). Evan - consent + subpoena playbook (due Fri). Carmen - pilot list + pricing constraints (due +7d). Liam - SOC2 evidence checklist (due +7d).
Noah (Eng): Got it. Will publish RFC updates to ops-bot link.
Priya (Security): Acknowledged.
Evan (Legal): Acknowledged.
Carmen (CS): Acknowledged.
Liam (Compliance): Acknowledged.
Rhea (PM): Thanks team. We'll reconvene next Tue. If anything urgent, ping @rhea on this thread. :calendar:
